front: Je finis, tu finis, il finit, nous finissons, vous finissez, ils finissent.
pronunciation: [zhuh fee-NEE, tü fee-NEE, eel fee-NEE, noo fee-nee-SOHN, voo fee-nee-SAY, eel fee-NEES]
back: I finish, you finish… they finish.
context: Model of regular -IR verbs (2nd group): -iss- appears in the plural. Like choisir, réussir, grandir.

front: Je finis le travail à dix-sept heures.
context: 'Finir' (to finish) is the model of the second group.

front: Nous choisissons le menu du jour.
back: We're choosing the menu of the day.
context: 'Choisir' = to choose: nous choisissons.
'Grandir' = to grow up. Many -IR verbs come from adjectives: grand → grandir, rouge → rougir.
'Réussir un examen' = to pass an exam. 'Passer un examen' = to TAKE an exam.
'Partir' is NOT like finir: je pars, nous partons (no -iss-). Same pattern: sortir, dormir, sentir.
'Sortir' = to go out: je sors, nous sortons.
'Dormir': je dors, tu dors, il dort, nous dormons.

front: Ça sent bon dans la cuisine !
back: It smells good in the kitchen!
context: 'Sentir' = to smell (and to feel). 'Se sentir bien' = to feel well.
'Venir': je viens, tu viens, il vient, nous venons, vous venez, ils viennent.
'Ils viennent' doubles the n. 'Venir de' + country.
Passé récent: venir de + infinitive = to have just done something.

back: I really want to thank you.
context: 'Tenir' (like venir): je tiens. 'Tenir à' = to really want to, to care about.

front: J'ouvre la fenêtre, il fait chaud.
back: I'll open the window, it's hot.
context: 'Ouvrir' ends in -ir but conjugates like an -ER verb: j'ouvre, tu ouvres.

front: Je prends le bus tous les matins.
pronunciation: [zhuh prahn luh BÜS too lay mah-TAN]
back: I take the bus every morning.
context: 'Prendre': je prends, nous prenons, ils prennent (double n).
Like prendre: comprendre, apprendre. 'Je comprends', 'ils comprennent'.
'Apprendre' = to learn (also to teach: 'apprendre quelque chose à quelqu'un').

front: J'attends le bus depuis vingt minutes.
back: I've been waiting for the bus for twenty minutes.
context: 'Attendre' = to wait for (no 'pour'): j'attends le bus. Regular -RE: j'attends, nous attendons.
'Entendre' = to hear. Regular -RE verb like attendre, répondre, vendre.

front: Il répond toujours très vite à mes messages.
pronunciation: [eel ray-POHN too-zhoor treh VEET ah may meh-SAHZH]
back: He always replies to my messages very quickly.
context: 'Répondre à' = to answer, reply to. 'Il répond': the d is silent.

front: Ils vendent des légumes bio au marché.
pronunciation: [eel VAHND day lay-güm BYOH oh mar-SHAY]
back: They sell organic vegetables at the market.
context: 'Ils vendent': the d is pronounced in the plural.
'Perdre' = to lose. Regular -RE.

front: Nous descendons à la prochaine station.
back: We're getting off at the next station.
context: 'Descendre' = to go down, get off. Regular -RE.
'Mettre' = to put: je mets, nous mettons. 'Mettre la table' = to set the table.

front: Qu'est-ce que tu mets pour la soirée ?
back: What are you wearing to the party?
context: 'Mettre' also means to put on (clothes).

front: Je lis le journal le matin.
back: I read the newspaper in the morning.
context: 'Lire': je lis, nous lisons, ils lisent.
'Écrire': j'écris, nous écrivons, ils écrivent.
'Dire': je dis, nous disons, but 'vous dites' (irregular, like 'vous faites').

front: Je connais un bon restaurant près d'ici.
pronunciation: [zhuh koh-neh an bohn res-toh-RAHN preh dee-SEE]
back: I know a good restaurant near here.
context: 'Connaître' = to know (people, places). 'Savoir' = to know (facts, how to).

front: Je sais nager, mais je ne connais pas cette plage.
pronunciation: [zhuh seh nah-ZHAY, meh zhuh nuh koh-neh pah set PLAZH]
back: I can swim, but I don't know this beach.
context: 'Savoir' + infinitive = to know how to. 'Connaître' + place or person.
'Pouvoir': je peux, nous pouvons, ils peuvent.

back: Do you want to come for dinner?
context: 'Vouloir': je veux, nous voulons, ils veulent.
'Devoir': je dois, nous devons, ils doivent.

front: Je bois un verre avec des amis.
pronunciation: [zhuh bwah an VEHR ah-vek day zah-MEE]
back: I'm having a drink with friends.
context: 'Boire': je bois, nous buvons, ils boivent. 'Boire un verre' = to have a drink.

front: Je crois que tu as raison.
context: 'Croire' (to believe): je crois, nous croyons. 'Je crois que' = I think that.
